answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Speech by the Team Captain

Good evening, Coach and my dear teammates,

I know how heavy our hearts are today. We dreamed of lifting the trophy at the First Inter School Football Competition, and we lost in the semi-final. It hurts. But let me remind you whom we lost to: the team that went on to become the champions. We gave them their toughest match of the tournament, and that is something to be proud of.

Let us first look at the positives. We reached the semi-final in our very first year in this competition. Our defence let in only two goals in four matches. Rohan's goalkeeping was outstanding, and our passing in the midfield was praised by the referees themselves. Above all, not one of us gave up, even when we were a goal down in the last ten minutes.

Now let us be honest about where we fell short. We missed three clear chances in front of the goal because we hurried our shots. Our stamina dropped in the second half, and their players were faster than us in the final twenty minutes. We also lost our shape at corners, which is how they scored the winning goal.

So here is our plan for the future. From next week, we will begin our practice half an hour earlier for running and fitness drills. Every forward will practise twenty shots on goal after each session. We will set aside one day a week to practise corners and free kicks, both in attack and in defence. Coach has also agreed to arrange friendly matches with stronger teams, so that we learn to play under pressure.

Teammates, a defeat is not the end; it is a lesson. Champions are not those who never fall, but those who rise every time they fall. Let us keep our heads high, work harder than ever, and come back next year to bring that trophy home.

Thank you.

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.finalAnswer: The writer's Research Methodology teacher; he tore off his class notes after each class and threw them away, so that he would not repeat today's knowledge in tomorrow's class, which would put him and the class to sleep.
answers.solution: The strange habit belongs to the writer's teacher who taught Research Methodology. After each class he tore off his class notes and threw them in the waste paper basket. He did this because if he kept the notes, he would only repeat what he knew that day in the next class, and that would put him and the whole class to sleep.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: What the teacher would learn tomorrow, that is, new learning.
answers.solution: The new things the teacher would learn the next day would keep him as well as his class awake. The teacher said, 'What I would learn tomorrow will keep me as well as the class, awake.'

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: A learned man holds on to old knowledge and thinks he knows all the answers; a man of learning stays curious, keeps asking questions and keeps learning about the present.
answers.solution: A learned man is stuck with what he learnt in the past. He thinks he already has all the answers, so his knowledge is like dead wood on an old, bent tree. A man of learning is curious about what is happening now. He keeps asking questions and learning new things, so he is lively and fresh, like a green twig pushing out of the soil after rain.

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: He has all the answers and no room for new questions or discoveries, so he only repeats old knowledge and makes learning dull.
answers.solution: A learned man has all the answers and no room in his head for new questions or discoveries. He keeps repeating old knowledge and only feeds the head, never touching the heart, so his teaching becomes dull and does not awaken anyone. In this way he can put a whole generation to sleep.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: The heart, the deepest point of our attention where head and heart meet; we point to it when we say 'I'.
answers.solution: The centre of awareness is the deepest point of our attention, which the writer places at the heart. When a person says 'I', he points towards his heart, because by Nature's design that is the centre of his awareness. 'Learning by heart' means going to this centre and paying deep attention, joining the head and the heart.

answers.label: Q.2(f)
answers.finalAnswer: To give up its secrets, if we only know how to knock and give it the necessary blow.
answers.solution: According to Swami Vivekananda, the world is ready to give up its secrets, if we only know how to knock and how to give it the necessary blow.

answers.label: Q.2(g)
answers.finalAnswer: It gives strength and force to our effort; the more concentrated the mind, the more power it brings to one point.
answers.solution: Concentration gives strength and force to the 'blow' that opens the world's secrets. The more concentrated the mind is, the more power it can bring to bear on one point. So concentration is the core of all learning.

answers.label: Q.2(h)
answers.finalAnswer: The more concentrated the mind is, the more power is brought to bear on one point.
answers.solution: The secret is the power of concentration: 'The more concentrated it (the mind) is, the more power is brought to bear on one point; that is the secret.' A concentrated mind can unlock the secrets of the world.

answers.label: Q.3(a)
answers.finalAnswer: Because old age should bring peace, ripeness and fulfilment, the reward of a life lived bravely and honestly, without bitterness or lies.
answers.solution: The poet feels it should be lovely to be old because old age ought to be full of the peace that comes from experience. A person who has lived bravely ('undaunted'), without becoming bitter ('unsoured') and without accepting lies, reaches a ripe, complete and satisfied old age, sweet and soothing like ripe apples.

answers.label: Q.3(b)
answers.finalAnswer: Simile
answers.solution: It is a simile, because old people are compared to yellowing leaves using the word 'like'.

answers.label: Q.3(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Going through all the good and bad times and hardships of life bravely.
answers.solution: 'Facing all weathers' means going through every kind of situation in life, good times and bad times, joys and hardships, and facing them all with courage. The young man admires his father for having lived such a full and brave life.

answers.label: Q.3(d)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) unrest (war); (ii) foul-smelling; (iii) rejected
answers.solution:
(i) peace: unrest (or war, disturbance)
(ii) fragrant: foul-smelling (or stinking)
(iii) accepted: rejected

answers.label: Q.3(e)
answers.finalAnswer: Not discouraged or frightened; fearless.
answers.solution: 'Undaunted' means not discouraged or frightened by difficulty or danger; fearless and determined.

answers.label: Q.3(f)
answers.finalAnswer: Beautiful Old Age
answers.solution: A suitable title is 'Beautiful Old Age' (or 'The Joy of Growing Old'), because the whole poem describes how lovely and peaceful old age should be after a life lived well.

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Topics chosen: (a) and (c).

(a) A rotten apple spoils the barrel

If one apple in a barrel begins to rot, it soon spoils the good apples around it. In the same way, one bad person can spoil a whole group. In a class, a single student who cheats, bullies or talks back to teachers can lead others to copy him. In a team, one lazy player can break the spirit of the rest. That is why parents ask us to choose our friends carefully. At the same time, the proverb reminds us of our own duty: we must not become the rotten apple. If a friend goes astray, we should try to help him change, and if he does not, we should keep away from his bad habits.

(c) Man proposes, God disposes

This proverb means that people can make plans, but the final result is not always in their hands. A farmer may plough his field and sow good seeds, yet a flood or a drought can destroy his crop. A student may prepare well for a match, and then fall ill on the day. Such events teach us to be humble. However, the proverb does not ask us to stop planning or working. It asks us to do our best and then accept the result calmly. If we fail in spite of our effort, we should not lose heart, but try again with faith and patience.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
From: arjun.sharma@gmail.com
To: riya.sharma@gmail.com
Date: 10 June 2021
Subject: What I learnt at summer camp

Dear Riya,

I am back from the ten-day summer camp at Mussoorie, and I have a lesson to share with you. Every morning we woke up at five and did exercises, a two-kilometre run and yoga. On the first day I was tired and wanted to sleep, but by the third day I felt fresh and full of energy. I could climb the hill on our trek without stopping, and I slept well every night. I now understand that daily exercise keeps both the body and the mind strong. Let us exercise together every morning from tomorrow.

Thanks and Regards,
Arjun

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
The Last Train

"We have plenty of time," said my elder brother Vivek, stretching lazily on the sofa. Our train to Delhi was at six in the evening, and it was only half past three.

Mother had packed our bags in the morning. All we had to do was reach the station, which was only twenty minutes away. So Vivek finished his cricket match on television, and I went to say goodbye to my friends next door.

At half past four, Father asked for the tickets. Vivek searched his pocket, then his bag, then the whole house. After twenty anxious minutes, we found them under the sofa cushion. We rushed out and waved at a taxi.

But the road was blocked by a long wedding procession, with a band playing and people dancing in the middle of the street. Our taxi crawled forward inch by inch. Vivek kept looking at his watch. "We will still make it," he whispered, though his face had turned pale.

At a quarter to six, we were still two kilometres away. The driver took a short cut through a narrow lane, only to find a cow sitting calmly in the middle of it. He honked again and again, but the cow did not move.

We reached the station at six minutes past six. We ran up the stairs with our heavy bags, and from the bridge we saw the red light at the back of our train slowly disappearing into the distance.

Vivek sat down on his suitcase and laughed weakly. Looking back at that long afternoon of television, lost tickets, the procession and the cow, I knew the truth: we were never going to make it.

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Theme chosen: (c) Pollution.

Pollution

The river once was clear and blue,
The morning air was fresh and new;
Now smoke and dust have filled the sky,
And birds have stopped their songs nearby.
The plastic floats on every stream,
The forests vanish like a dream.
If we plant trees and save each drop,
The poison in the air will stop.
So let us act, both young and old,
To save this earth more dear than gold.

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: (a) missing 'with', preposition, between 'happy' and 'us'; (b) hardly -> hard, adverb; (c) wisely -> wisdom, noun; (d) missing 'them', pronoun, between 'Let' and 'do'; (e) do -> don't, auxiliary verb; (f) jump -> step, noun; (g) missing 'and', conjunction, between 'Ramesh' and 'Renu'; (h) Alas -> Hurrah, interjection; (i) missing 'much', adjective, between 'How' and 'money'; (j) gets -> get, verb
answers.solution:
(a) Missing word: with. Part of speech: preposition. Location: between 'happy' and 'us'. (He is very happy with us.)
(b) Incorrect word: hardly. Correct word: hard. Part of speech: adverb. ('Hardly' means 'almost not'.)
(c) Incorrect word: wisely. Correct word: wisdom. Part of speech: noun. (It must match the noun 'patience'.)
(d) Missing word: them. Part of speech: pronoun. Location: between 'Let' and 'do'. (Let them do whatever they want.)
(e) Incorrect word: do. Correct word: don't. Part of speech: auxiliary (helping) verb. A positive statement takes a negative question tag: 'They know about your plans, don't they?'
(f) Incorrect word: jump. Correct word: step. Part of speech: noun. (The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.)
(g) Missing word: and. Part of speech: conjunction. Location: between 'Ramesh' and 'Renu'.
(h) Incorrect word: Alas. Correct word: Hurrah. Part of speech: interjection. 'Alas' shows sorrow; winning calls for joy.
(i) Missing word: much. Part of speech: adjective. Location: between 'How' and 'money'. (How much money do you want?)
(j) Incorrect word: gets (the second one). Correct word: get. Part of speech: verb. 'The tough' means tough people, which is plural: 'When the going gets tough, the tough get going.'

answers.label: Q.9
answers.finalAnswer: (a) in the pink; (b) the white feather; (c) saw red; (d) the nod; (e) as black as he is painted; (f) pulled off; (g) took to; (h) paid off; (i) came round; (j) acts upon
answers.solution:
(a) He is now in the pink (of health). ('in the pink' = in good health)
(b) Vikram never showed the white feather in his life. ('show the white feather' = act like a coward)
(c) The teacher saw red when the naughty boy disturbed others in the class. ('see red' = become very angry)
(d) If we request him, he will definitely give us the nod. ('give the nod' = give permission)
(e) He is not as black as he is painted. ('not as black as one is painted' = not as bad as people say)
(f) The underdog pulled off a stunning victory. ('pull off' = succeed in something difficult)
(g) The actor took to drinking when his movies did not do well. ('take to' = begin a habit)
(h) Dhoni's plan to deceive the batsman paid off. ('pay off' = succeed)
(i) Very soon he came round (or came to). ('come round' = become conscious again)
(j) His parents love him because he always acts upon (or acts on) their advice. ('act upon' = follow)

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: (a) He is better than most other athletes in the country.; (b) She said that it was time they left the class.; (c) Is there anyone who is not a fan of Neeraj Chopra?; (d) No sooner did he throw the javelin than he started celebrating.; (e) Why was the house located in the village renovated by his people?; (f) We all saw your bravery.; (g) Despite being given less time to study, he came first in the exam.; (h) The boys said, "Let us go and swim in the river."; (i) The girl was too happy on her birthday to think of her exams.; (j) The boy who is wearing a jacket knows where the sweets have been kept.
answers.solution:
(a) He is better than most other athletes in the country.
(b) She said that it was time they left the class. ('It is time' becomes 'it was time'; 'we' becomes 'they'.)
(c) Is there anyone who is not a fan of Neeraj Chopra?
(d) No sooner did he throw the javelin than he started celebrating.
(e) Why was the house located in the village renovated by his people?
(f) We all saw your bravery.
(g) Despite being given less time to study, he came first in the exam.
(h) The boys said, "Let us go and swim in the river."
(i) The girl was too happy on her birthday to think of her exams. (One finite verb only, so it is a simple sentence.)
(j) The boy who is wearing a jacket knows where the sweets have been kept.

Note: the paper spells 'javeline'; the correct spelling is 'javelin'. In (d), the usual change of 'As soon as' to a negative form is 'No sooner ... than'.

answers.label: Q.11
answers.finalAnswer: (a) Isolate; (b) Straight forward; (c) Oppose; (d) Fresh; (e) Hidden
answers.solution:
(a) Integrate: (i) Isolate. Sentence: The patient with the infection was isolated from the others.
(b) Enigmatic (mysterious): (iv) Straight forward. Sentence: Ravi gave a straightforward answer to every question.
(c) Concur (agree): (iii) Oppose. Sentence: The villagers opposed the plan to cut down the forest.
(d) Putrid (rotten): (i) Fresh. Sentence: My mother buys fresh vegetables every morning.
(e) Explicit (clearly stated): (iii) Hidden. Sentence: There was a hidden meaning in his words.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.finalAnswer: NATION; RATION; NATIONAL; RATIONAL; INTERNAL; ORIENTAL; TRAIN; TOTAL; LATENT; LINEAR
answers.solution:
INTERNATIONAL has the letters I (2), N (3), T (2), E (1), R (1), A (2), O (1), L (1).
Ten words of five or more letters, none using a letter more often than this:
1. NATION
2. RATION
3. NATIONAL
4. RATIONAL
5. INTERNAL
6. ORIENTAL
7. TRAIN
8. TOTAL

answers.label: Q.13
answers.finalAnswer: (a) with -> in; (b) too -> very; (c) Beside -> Besides; (d) in -> at; (e) must -> should
answers.solution:
(a) Error: with. Correction: in. (His uncle deals in rice: a trader 'deals in' goods.)
(b) Error: too. Correction: very. ('Too' means 'more than enough' and needs a reason after it.)
(c) Error: Beside. Correction: Besides. ('Besides' means 'in addition to'; 'beside' means 'next to'.)
(d) Error: in. Correction: at. (good at painting)
(e) Error: must. Correction: should. ('Lest' is followed by 'should'.)

answers.label: Q.14
answers.finalAnswer: (a) United we stand, divided we fall.; (b) One rotten apple spoils the whole barrel.; (c) Make hay while the sun shines.; (d) Rome was not built in a day.; (e) Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
answers.solution:
(a) United we stand, divided we fall.
(b) One rotten apple spoils the whole barrel. (Also: A man is known by the company he keeps.)
(c) Make hay while the sun shines. (Also: A stitch in time saves nine.)
(d) Rome was not built in a day.
(e) Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
